metadata.title: Access Control Reference
metadata.description: Complete reference for Capgo's role-based access control system — every role, every permission, the hierarchy, and how to assign roles via API and CLI.

When an App Preview key creates a channel, Capgo automatically gives that key a child
binding for the new channel only:
Read the channel created by the key
Set the key's own uploaded bundle on that channel
, the key may enumerate channel metadata in the selected app. The automatic child binding is a
boundary: it does not grant lifecycle mutations for a channel the key did not create.

Capgo records the preview key that created each channel and uploaded each bundle. Therefore an App Preview key can create each non-public preview channel it needs, promote its own bundle, and atomically delete that channel and bundle with
; it cannot do those things to an existing default/main channel, another preview key's channel, or another key's bundle.

:::caution
Every App Preview binding remains linked to the selected app's owning organization. The role omits an organization-wide role; it does not remove the organization association. Revoking or expiring the app binding removes the key's effective lifecycle access.
:::

Each permission can be set to:
— inherit from the app role (the default)
— explicitly grant, regardless of the app role
— explicitly block, regardless of the app role
This lets you, for example, give an App Reader the ability to associate bundles on the
channel without promoting them to App Developer.

Instead of assigning roles to each user individually, you can create
and assign roles to the group. Every member of the group inherits those roles automatically.
Groups can hold role bindings at

When a user's permissions are evaluated, all their group memberships are resolved transparently. If any of their groups grants the required permission, access is allowed.
, and permissions from all groups are additive.
— API keys do not inherit group roles.
5 QA engineers need Developer access to 3 apps
All group endpoints require authentication and are served under

curl -X POST "https://api.capgo.app/private/groups/<ORG_ID>" \
  -H "authorization: <API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "QA Team",
    "description": "Quality assurance engineers"
  }'
Deleting a group also removes all its role bindings. Members are not deleted from the organization.
